The request paths of TC-B1-003 and TC-B1-004 are built from the mutable class-static field pathId instead of the canonical literals "/students/5" (INPUT-B1-003-01-2) and "/students/0" (INPUT-B1-004-01-2). tcB1003 reads pathId (5) and then sets it to 0; tcB1004 expects pathId to already be 0. JUnit 5 does not guarantee declaration order, and a single or repeated run of either method sends the other case's path while asserting its own id, so the tests are order-dependent and can fail against a correct application. Bind both paths as literals and remove the shared state.

The request path of TC-B1-003 and TC-B1-004 is built from a mutable static field pathId (L035, initial 5) instead of the canonical literals "/students/5" and "/students/0"; tcB1003 mutates it to 0 (L117) and tcB1004 relies on that side effect (L126). With JUnit 5 default (non-declaration) method ordering, or when tcB1004 runs alone, it sends GET /students/5 and L129 fails; the tests are order-dependent and their input bindings drift from the canonical inputs. Rework: use the literal paths and remove the static field.

TC-B1-003 and TC-B1-004 build the request path from a shared mutable static field instead of the canonical literals. StudentControllerPipelineTest L035 declares private static int pathId = 5; tcB1003 (L116) requests "/students/" + pathId and then sets pathId = 0 (L117); tcB1004 (L126) requests "/students/" + pathId and asserts id 0. INPUT-B1-003-01-2 is the literal "/students/5" and INPUT-B1-004-01-2 is "/students/0"; neither literal appears in the code. The outcome depends on execution order (JUnit 5 default order is not declaration order and the class has no @TestMethodOrder) and on JVM history: run first, tcB1004 sends /students/5 and fails on id; rerun in the same JVM, tcB1003 sends /students/0 and fails. This violates deterministic data and order independence and is a literal/binding drift requiring rework: use the canonical path literals directly and remove the static field.

TC-B1-004 does not bind the canonical path literal "/students/0" (INPUT-B1-004-01-2). SYMBOL-B1-004 builds the path from the static field pathId (initialised to 5) that SYMBOL-B1-003 mutates to 0 after its own request. The outcome of TC-B1-004 therefore depends on TC-B1-003 running first; with JUnit 5 default method ordering (not declaration order) or when run alone, the request becomes GET /students/5 and ASSERT-B1-004-01-1-2 (expected id 0) fails. Independence from execution order is violated and the input literal drifts; rework required: bind "/students/0" directly and remove the mutable static.
